whatItDoes: Projects how a lump sum plus regular monthly contributions grows over time with compound interest. Shows the matured value, the total amount contributed, and the interest earned on top, so you can see exactly how much of the final balance is your own money versus growth.
whyItExists: Compound interest is the engine behind long-term saving, but the numbers are easy to underestimate. A calculator turns the compound growth formula into an instant projection so investors can see what small monthly amounts become over decades.
whoShouldUse: Long-term savers, retirement planners, students learning about investing, financial advisors, and anyone comparing lump-sum deposits against systematic monthly investing.
useCases: Project how much a fixed deposit or index fund grows with monthly additions
Compare lump-sum investing vs. equal monthly contributions over the same horizon
Estimate the future value of a retirement fund decades from now
See how interest earned exceeds contributions over long horizons
Model an education or down-payment savings goal with monthly top-ups
Demonstrate to younger savers why starting early beats investing more later
instructions: Enter your starting amount in Initial amount
Add a monthly contribution to model ongoing savings, or set it to 0 for a pure lump sum
Set the expected annual interest rate in percent
Choose the number of years you will let it grow
Read the matured value, total contributed, and interest earned
Adjust any input and watch the projection update so you can test scenarios
examples: $10,000 initial, $500/month at 7% for 30 years → ~$150,000 contributed but ~$650,000+ matured thanks to compounding
bestPractices: Use a conservative rate estimate and review it periodically as markets change
Recall that the projection is pre-tax and pre-inflation — real returns will be lower
Increase your contribution when income grows; small raises compound a lot over decades
Treat the total interest figure as the bonus earned over your own contributions
Check both the 10-year and 30-year numbers to appreciate the power of time
commonMistakes: Ignoring fees and taxes that reduce actual returns
Assuming a single high rate will hold for the entire period
Comparing nominal values without adjusting for inflation
Entering interest as a decimal (0.07 instead of 7)
Forgetting that withdrawing early resets the compounding curve
faq: Does this assume the rate compounds monthly? — Yes, interest is compounded monthly by default.
Is this financial advice? — No, it is a projection purely for planning; always consult a qualified advisor.
Do I have to enter a monthly contribution? — No, set it to 0 to model a single lump sum.
Is my data sent anywhere? — No, all calculations run in your browser.
Why does the interest column grow so much in year 20? — Because each year's interest is earned on all previous interest, so growth accelerates over time.
What rate should I use? — Historically, diversified long-term equity has returned roughly 7-10% nominal annually, but past performance does not guarantee future results.
features: Initial deposit and recurring contribution support
Total invested and interest earned breakdown
Instant scenario testing across rates and terms
assumptions: Generic compound interest calculation; no country-specific assumptions.
